newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE nearby canola down on funds, crushers buy Nov.
newsitem.headline: WCE nearby canola down on funds, crushers buy Nov.

text.p: WCE nearby canola ended down on fund selling while crushers bought November, traders said.

"Funds sold 400 July, their short totals 3,200 now, locals sold. Crushers bought November and January," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin rose to -2.35 Wednesday from -4.75 Tuesday. July-Nov spread from $30 to $27. Volume was 5,245 lots, or 104,900 tonnes, with 383 hedge lots.
Japan bought 10,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
July canola lost $0.50 to close at $409 and November up $2.10 to $381.50.
UGG sold 400 July flax down $0.10 to $331 to PCTS and September ended up $0.70 at $322.50 as UGG sold, traders said.
July feed wheat up $0.70 to $159 on commercial buying and October rose $1.50 to $161.50. Volume was 269 lots.
Commercials bought July western barley up $1.30 at $136, Midland Walwyn was the best buyer of October as PCTS bought also with October ended up $1 at $136.50. Volume was 350.
Expectations the Canadian Wheat Board will increase its world barley price outlook in Thursday May Pool Return Outlook at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT buoyed WCE barley, traders said.
RBC-DS sold July feed peas down the US$5 limit to US$196.50 and UGG sold 100 December feed pea contracts down US$3.50 at US$188.50, traders said. Volume was 155.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
